chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The minimum of the menstruation (haydh) is three days, and the maximum is ten days.

key_terms.أقل: Minimum threshold — the fewest days that can legally constitute haydh
key_terms.أكثر: Maximum threshold — the most days that can legally constitute haydh
key_terms.الحيض: Haydh — menstruation; a state of ritual impurity (najasah) that suspends obligatory prayer and fasting

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum and maximum duration of haydh (menstruation) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the jurisprudential boundaries for menstrual bleeding: a minimum of three days and a maximum of ten days. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh, as it determines when a woman's ritual obligations (such as prayer and fasting) are suspended or resumed. The hadith is transmitted through a strong chain via the prominent jurist-transmitter Muawiya ibn Ammar, one of al-Sadiq's most trusted students for fiqh matters.
